<description>
This PR catches two birds with one stone:

- fixes https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/36515
- adds a `Block` interface, which lets IPC clients fetch the block data (or its header)

This means a client can still fetch (and store) the block after `submitSolution()`, but we no longer mutate the template's `CBlock` for this.

### Block interface

`submitSolution()` no longer modifies the template. It applies the solution to a copy of the template block and returns a `Block` handle for that copy, also when the block is rejected.

`Mining::submitBlock()` and `BlockTemplate::block()` do the same. The new interface has a `data()`, `header()` and `coinbaseMerklePath()` method, so these are migrated from the `BlockTemplate` interface.

The interface can be expanded later, e.g. to tell whether the block is part of the active chain (or went stale, useful for a miner to know).

This is a breaking change for IPC clients:

- `getBlockHeader()` → `block().header()`
- `getBlock()` → `block().data()`
- `getCoinbaseMerklePath()` → `block().coinbaseMerklePath()`
- `bool submitSolution(..., reason, debug)` → `Block submitSolution(..., accepted, reason, debug)`
- `bool submitBlock(block, reason, debug)` → `Block submitBlock(block, accepted, reason, debug)`

It uses new ordinals and old methods throw.

`submitSolution()` now throws when the coinbase is null, instead of returning false.

### Performance

My agent measured how long after `submitSolution()` sv2-tp forwards the next template, with master as the baseline and an adapted sv2-tp as the client:

| Workload | Master | This PR | Paired median difference (95% CI) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Empty block | 1.32 ms | 1.40 ms | +0.05 ms [−0.11, +0.15] |
| Near-full block, 3.7 MB | 10.11 ms | 10.07 ms | −0.09 ms [−0.44, +0.28] |

The extra `block()` call costs about 0.15 ms per template for a C++ client. The alternative approach of having `submitSolution()` return the full `CBlock` added 6ms.
</description>

@ViniciusCestarii looking into your approach
[2026-11-18] c:6982149571 comment by Sjors (member):
I added a new `Block` interface. To keep this PR simple, I'm going to open a fresh PR for `getTotalFees()`, since it no longer makes sense to combine that feature (requested in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35671#issuecomment-6165435275) with the fix for https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/36515. Most review on this PR was focussed on the latter.

The `Block` interface is returned by `submitSolution()`, `submitBlock()` and `getBlock()`. It starts out with just `data()`, `header()` and `coinbaseMerklePath()`. The latter two are moved out of `BlockTemplate`.

It could later be expanded later to e.g. say if a block is part of the active chain (very useful for a miner to know).

The `coinbaseTx()` getter stays on the template, because it does not return the actual coinbase transaction but rather a struct that is only useful for mining software to _generate_ a coinbase transaction.

I'm keeping `getTxFees()` and `getTxSigops()` in the template, because they are calculated at template generation time and non-trivial to calculate in other contexts.

The chain interface proposed in #29409 might also be able to use this.

I renamed `getBlock()` to `block()`, so clients call `block().data()` to get the block's data. Note that this takes advantage of Cap’n Proto promise pipelining (see the `ipc_util.py` change).

This is a breaking change and I intentionally made `getBlockOld2`, etc fail, because in the past reviewers complained when I made backward compatible changes while the interface is still experimental. This is no problem for sv2-tp and SRI which are pretty good at handling our breaking changes between our major releases. (FWIW my goal is to remove the experimental status after Windows support lands)

I ran the performance benchmark again and there's no regression, so: a better interface, no need for a mutex and it stays fast.
